title: An uncancelled polynomial denominator root bounds the convergence radius
statement:
Let $P,Q\in\mathbf C[T]$ be polynomials [def-weil-polynomial-ring], let $f=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in\mathbf C[[T]]$ be a formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series], and regard polynomials as power series by [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Suppose $Q(0)\ne0$ and $Qf=P$ in $\mathbf C[[T]]$. For $a\in\mathbf C$ satisfying $Q(a)=0$ and $P(a)\ne0$, the convergence radius $R(f)$ of [d-real-series] satisfies
$$R(f)\leq |a|,$$
where $|a|$ is the complex absolute value [def-weil-complex-absolute-value].

source.place: Final paragraph, Taylor-radius conclusion; the general polynomial identity formulation isolates its analytic input.

proof.text: Assume for contradiction that $R(f)>|a|$. By the definition of $R(f)$ in [d-real-series], the numerical series $\sum_{n\ge0}|c_n|\,|a|^n$ converges, so $f(a)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_na^n$ is well-defined and absolutely convergent. Write $Q=\sum_{k=0}^d q_kT^k$. The formal identity $Qf=P$, using the coefficient convolution in [def-weil-formal-power-series] and the polynomial-to-series map [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series], says that the coefficients of $P$ are those of this Cauchy product. Since the sum over $k$ is finite and the series for $f(a)$ is absolutely convergent, evaluating that product at $a$ gives $P(a)=Q(a)f(a)=0$. This contradicts $P(a)\ne0$. Hence $R(f)\le |a|$.
